exact.✔ 正確！LDA 共享共變異數 → 線性邊界、參數少、穩健。QDA 會過度彈性。: ✔ Correct! LDA shares one covariance → linear boundary, few parameters, robust. QDA would be overly flexible.
exact.✔ 正確！Logistic 直接估 P(Y|X)，判別式、機率可校準；Bayes: ✔ Correct! Logistic regression estimates P(Y|X) directly: it is discriminative and its probabilities can be calibrated; Bayes/LDA are generative.
exact.✔ 正確！蚊香屬於非線性不可分，核技巧映射到高維線性分離最優雅。: ✔ Correct! A mosquito-coil spiral is not linearly separable; the most elegant fix is the kernel trick, which maps the data to a high-dimensional space where it becomes linearly separable.
exact.✔ 正確！Bagging + 特徵隨機抽樣讓樹去相關，平均後大幅壓制變異。: ✔ Correct! Bagging + random feature sampling decorrelates the trees, so averaging them suppresses the variance dramatically.
exact.✗ 再想想：此假設下 LDA 的線性邊界最穩健，QDA 與核方法過於彈性。: ✗ Think again: under this assumption LDA's linear boundary is the most robust; QDA and kernel methods are too flexible.
exact.✗ 提示：誰是「不管生成、直接算條件機率」的那一派？: ✗ Hint: which camp "ignores how the data are generated and computes the conditional probability directly"?
exact.✗ 提示：調 k 或先驗解決不了幾何纏繞，需要改變表示或映射。: ✗ Hint: tuning k or the prior can't undo geometric entanglement; you need to change the representation or the mapping.
exact.✗ 提示：關鍵是「去相關後平均」如何影響變異。: ✗ Hint: the key is how "averaging after decorrelating" affects the variance.

e8841eb3bbd8.zh:
給電腦一堆線索，
它憑什麼敢拍板「這是 A 還是 B」？ Given a pile of clues, what gives a machine the right to declare “it’s A, not B”?
e8841eb3bbd8.en:
Give a computer a pile of clues:
what gives it the nerve to rule “this is A, not B”?

bb17aa10abf4.zh: 答案不只一種——有人講「成見＋證據」，有人直接硬切一刀，有人問鄰居，有人把世界摺到高維再切。There is no single answer: some combine prior & evidence, some cut a hard boundary, some ask neighbours, some lift the world to higher dimensions.
bb17aa10abf4.en: There is more than one answer: some talk about “prior belief + evidence,” some just make one hard cut, some ask the neighbors, and some fold the world into a higher dimension and then cut.

9131c8aaf6d7.zh: 分類是什麼？不只是貼標籤 What Is Classification? Not Just Labeling
9131c8aaf6d7.en: What Is Classification? It's More Than Sticking On Labels

3c3fe0f54395.zh: 分類就是「在不確定下做決定」的科學。輸入是特徵向量 $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$，輸出是離散標籤 $y \in \{C_1,\dots,C_K\}$。關鍵在於：不同家族對「不確定」有完全不同的建模方式。Classification = decision under uncertainty: input $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, output label $y$. Families differ in how they model uncertainty.
3c3fe0f54395.en: Classification is the science of “making decisions under uncertainty.” The input is a feature vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, and the output is a discrete label $y \in \{C_1,\dots,C_K\}$. The key point: different families model “uncertainty” in completely different ways.

866dae32d0dc.zh: 生成式 (Generative)：先學會「每類長什麼樣」$P(X\mid C_j)$，再用貝氏算後驗。Learn $P(X\mid C_j)$ per class, then posterior via Bayes.
866dae32d0dc.en: Generative: first learn “what each class looks like,” $P(X\mid C_j)$, then compute the posterior with Bayes' rule.

d80c93158eb0.zh: 判別式 (Discriminative)：不管怎麼生成，直接學邊界 $P(Y\mid X)$ 或決策函數。Ignore generation; learn $P(Y\mid X)$ or boundary directly.
d80c93158eb0.en: Discriminative: never mind how the data is generated; learn the boundary $P(Y\mid X)$ or a decision function directly.

35bed9572e39.zh: 三種邊界長相 Three boundary shapes

c4767f8c8e96.zh: 直線（LDA / Logistic / SVM 線性）、二次曲線（QDA / 核 SVM）、階梯狀（決策樹）。Linear, quadratic, staircase — each reflects an assumption about the world.
c4767f8c8e96.en: Straight lines (LDA / logistic regression / linear SVM), quadratic curves (QDA / kernel SVM), staircases (decision trees).

65a808b5a2aa.zh: 沒有萬能模型，只有「對的假設配對的資料」。No free lunch: right assumption must match the data.
65a808b5a2aa.en: There is no universal model, only “the right assumption paired with the right data.”

39f184a537a9.zh: 一句話記住六大家族 One-liner per family
39f184a537a9.en: Remember the six families in one sentence each

67106b274442.zh: 貝氏：成見＋證據；LDA/QDA：胖瘦決定直或彎；Logistic：直接算機率；KNN：問鄰居；樹/森林：官僚流程＋投票；SVM：留最寬安全島。Bayes priors+evidence; LDA/QDA covariance decides line/curve; Logistic direct prob; KNN neighbours vote; Trees bureaucracy+ensemble; SVM widest margin.
67106b274442.en: Bayes: prior belief + evidence; LDA/QDA: fat or thin decides straight or curved; logistic regression: compute the probability directly; KNN: ask the neighbors; trees/forests: a bureaucratic flowchart + voting; SVM: leave the widest safety island.

c54a2de9df8a.zh: 先驗的威力 Power of priors

f2299c08eaa6.zh: 同一個 $x=5$，先驗 $0.5$:$0.5$ 時邊界在中間；先驗 $0.9$:$0.1$ 時後驗直接偏向多數——成見會吃掉證據。Same $x=5$: equal priors → boundary at centre; 0.9 vs 0.1 → majority dominates. Priors can swallow evidence.
f2299c08eaa6.en: For the same $x=5$, with priors $0.5$:$0.5$ the boundary sits in the middle; with priors $0.9$:$0.1$ the posterior leans straight toward the majority. Prior belief can swallow the evidence.

9c13f87786d1.zh: 把分類想成法庭：貝氏是「法官綜合前科（先驗）與現場跡證（似然）判案」；Logistic 是「陪審團只看現場投票給機率」；KNN 是「問隔壁鄰居你是哪幫的」；SVM 是「在兩幫之間劃最寬的無人區」。Courtroom: Bayes = judge (record + evidence), Logistic = jury voting prob, KNN = ask neighbours, SVM = widest no-man’s-land.
9c13f87786d1.en: Think of classification as a courtroom: Bayes is “a judge who weighs the defendant's record (the prior) together with the evidence at the scene (the likelihood) to decide the case”; logistic regression is “a jury that looks only at the scene and votes a probability”; KNN is “asking the next-door neighbors which gang you belong to”; SVM is “drawing the widest no-man's-land between the two gangs.”

0af0a1c2be40.zh: 1 · 貝氏家族：證據 × 成見 Bayes Family — Evidence × Prior

b62f7f27d115.zh: 老祖宗 Thomas Bayes 留下一條「綜合判斷」公式：後驗 $\propto$ 似然 $\times$ 先驗。理論上這是無敵的最優分類器（Bayes Optimal），實務上難在估準 $P(X\mid C_j)$。Bayes rule: posterior $\propto$ likelihood $\times$ prior — optimal in theory, hard to estimate in practice.
b62f7f27d115.en: The founding father, Thomas Bayes, left us a formula for “weighing it all together”: posterior $\propto$ likelihood $\times$ prior. In theory this is the unbeatable optimal classifier (Bayes optimal); in practice, the hard part is estimating $P(X\mid C_j)$ accurately.

ab983d8ab5e3.zh: 分母 $P(X=x)=\sum_k P(X\mid C_k)P(C_k)$ 只是歸一化常數，決策時比大小 $ \arg\max_j P(C_j\mid X)$ 即可。Denominator is normalization; decide by $\arg\max$ posterior.
ab983d8ab5e3.en: The denominator $P(X=x)=\sum_k P(X\mid C_k)P(C_k)$ is just a normalizing constant; to decide, just compare sizes: $ \arg\max_j P(C_j\mid X)$.

bee8fa148d2b.en: How well does the scene fit?

24ae0bdeccd4.zh: 證據 Evidence  P(X) = Σ  Likelihood·Prior  (歸一化)

a5637b6e5325.zh: 貝氏思維：成見與證據相乘後歸一化，再取最大後驗 · Bayes: prior × likelihood → normalized posterior → argmax
a5637b6e5325.en: Bayesian thinking: multiply prior belief by evidence, normalize, then take the maximum posterior

39e7a1a7f310.zh: 四個名詞一次記牢 · Four Terms
39e7a1a7f310.en: Four Terms to Remember Once and for All

58a85586ad2a.zh:
後驗 $P(C_j\mid X)$：看到 $x$ 後兇手是 $j$ 的機率（要算的答案）。
先驗 $P(C_j)$：還沒看現場前的成見。
似然 $P(X\mid C_j)$：若兇手是 $j$，現場長這樣的機率。
證據 $P(X)$：所有人留下此跡證的總機率（分母）。Posterior = answer; prior = belief before seeing $x$; likelihood = how typical $x$ is under $C_j$; evidence = normalizer.
58a85586ad2a.en:
Posterior $P(C_j\mid X)$: the probability that the culprit is $j$ after seeing $x$ (the answer we want).
Prior $P(C_j)$: the preconception before looking at the scene.
Likelihood $P(X\mid C_j)$: if the culprit is $j$, the probability that the scene looks like this.
Evidence $P(X)$: the total probability that anyone would leave this trace (the denominator).

944d176dd2c4.zh: 為何需要 Naive Bayes？ · Why Naive?
944d176dd2c4.en: Why Do We Need Naive Bayes?

834cb833118d.zh: 特徵維度 $d$ 一高，$P(X\mid C_j)$ 估不準。乾脆假設特徵條件獨立：$P(X\mid C_j)=\prod_i P(X_i\mid C_j)$——天真但常很能打，尤其文本分類。High $d$ → density hard to estimate. Naive assumes conditional independence — often surprisingly strong, esp. text.
834cb833118d.en: Once the feature dimension $d$ gets high, $P(X\mid C_j)$ can't be estimated accurately. So just assume the features are conditionally independent: $P(X\mid C_j)=\prod_i P(X_i\mid C_j)$. Naive, but it often packs a punch, especially in text classification.

ff8ca0e0ad4b.zh: 動手算算看 · Worked Example（$X=5$ 站在兩群正中間）
ff8ca0e0ad4b.en: Let's Work It Out · Worked Example ($X=5$ stands right between the two groups)

15ff8a8f4e4a.zh: 設 $C_1\sim\mathcal{N}(3,1)$、$C_2\sim\mathcal{N}(7,1)$，先驗各 $0.5$，常態密度 $f(x)=\frac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}\exp(-\frac{(x-\mu)^2}{2\sigma^2})$。Two Gaussians $\mathcal{N}(3,1)$ vs $\mathcal{N}(7,1)$, equal priors, test $x=5$.
15ff8a8f4e4a.en: Let $C_1\sim\mathcal{N}(3,1)$ and $C_2\sim\mathcal{N}(7,1)$, with priors of $0.5$ each, and the normal density $f(x)=\frac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}\exp(-\frac{(x-\mu)^2}{2\sigma^2})$.

5bc6581749c3.zh:
$P(X=5\mid C_1)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-2}\approx 0.054$
$P(X=5\mid C_2)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-2}\approx 0.054$
兩邊距中心皆 $2\sigma$，對稱相等。Symmetric: both $2\sigma$ away → equal.
5bc6581749c3.en:
$P(X=5\mid C_1)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-2}\approx 0.054$
$P(X=5\mid C_2)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-2}\approx 0.054$
Both are $2\sigma$ from their centers, so by symmetry they are equal.

a9b1f9287878.zh:
$P(X)=0.054\cdot0.5+0.054\cdot0.5=0.054$
$P(C_1\mid5)=\frac{0.054\cdot0.5}{0.054}=0.5$
$P(C_2\mid5)=0.5$ → 邊界恰在 $x^*=5$Equal priors → boundary at mid-point $x^*=5$.

fa69da7e5691.zh: 💡 若先驗改為 $P(C_1)=0.9$，則 $P(C_1\mid5)=0.9$、$P(C_2\mid5)=0.1$——成見直接把邊界拉向少數類，即使似然相等也一面倒。With $0.9$ vs $0.1$ priors, posterior becomes $0.9$ — prior drags boundary toward minority.
fa69da7e5691.en: 💡 If the prior is changed to $P(C_1)=0.9$, then $P(C_1\mid5)=0.9$ and $P(C_2\mid5)=0.1$: the prior belief pulls the boundary straight toward the minority class, so even with equal likelihoods the decision is completely one-sided.

3893d7756044.zh: 貝氏決策邊界與後驗分佈圖 Bayes Boundary & Posterior — Interactive Demo
3893d7756044.en: Bayes Decision Boundary and Posterior Plot Interactive Demo

18f9ae7fe7aa.zh: 藍曲線 $C_1\sim\mathcal{N}(3,1)$、紅曲線 $C_2\sim\mathcal{N}(7,1)$。下方拉動先驗 $P(C_1)$，觀察加權密度與決策邊界如何被「成見」拉走。Blue $C_1$ vs red $C_2$. Drag the prior slider — weighted densities and boundary shift with belief.
18f9ae7fe7aa.en: Blue curve $C_1\sim\mathcal{N}(3,1)$, red curve $C_2\sim\mathcal{N}(7,1)$. Drag the prior $P(C_1)$ below and watch how the weighted densities and the decision boundary get pulled away by “bias”.

499ab45d6693.zh: 似然 × 先驗 → 後驗分佈（可調先驗） · Likelihood × Prior → Posterior

d138e6be250c.zh: 先驗 Prior $P(C_1)$ (drag to see prior power)：
d138e6be250c.en: Prior $P(C_1)$ (drag to see the power of the prior):

e52ca5a5f36e.zh: 決策邊界 x* ≈ 5.00 · Posterior at x=5: 0.50 / 0.50
e52ca5a5f36e.en: Decision boundary x* ≈ 5.00 · Posterior at x=5: 0.50 / 0.50

032abe474083.zh: 怎麼讀圖 · How to Read

33441669bdf0.zh: 實線是「長相」似然；虛線是用先驗加權後的高度。黑虛線是後驗 $0.5$ 的決策邊界——等高點。先驗一偏，虛線高低立變，邊界跟著平移。Solid = likelihood shape; dashed = prior-weighted. Black dashed = posterior $0.5$ boundary — equal posterior. Shift prior → weighted heights move → boundary slides.
33441669bdf0.en: The solid lines are the “looks” likelihoods; the dashed lines are their heights after weighting by the prior. The black dashed line is the decision boundary where the posterior is $0.5$: the point of equal height. Tilt the prior and the dashed heights change at once, and the boundary shifts along with them.

d98984a43ec7.zh: 當 $P(C_1)=0.9$，即使 $x=5$ 距兩中心等距，後驗仍 $0.9$ 壓倒 $0.1$。在不平衡資料（如詐欺 1%），忽略先驗會造成災難性誤判。With $0.9$ vs $0.1$, same $x=5$ gives $0.9$ vs $0.1$ posterior. Ignoring priors on imbalanced data is catastrophic.
d98984a43ec7.en: When $P(C_1)=0.9$, even though $x=5$ is equidistant from both centers, the posterior is still $0.9$, overwhelming $0.1$. On imbalanced data (e.g. 1% fraud), ignoring the prior leads to catastrophic misclassification.

9a14c617e900.zh: S2 · 幾何變形雙雄 · GEOMETRY

ebd1306f95a8.zh: LDA 與 QDA：胖瘦決定直或彎 LDA vs QDA — Covariance Decides Linear or Curved
ebd1306f95a8.en: LDA and QDA: Plump or Slim Decides Straight or Curved Covariance Decides Linear or Curved

b134a320d1e1.zh: 兩者皆假設每類是高斯，差在「胖瘦是否相同」。共變異數相等 → 線性超平面；各異 → 二次曲線。Both assume Gaussian per class; equal covariance → linear, unequal → quadratic.
b134a320d1e1.en: Both assume each class is Gaussian; the difference is whether they are “equally plump”. Equal covariances → a linear hyperplane; different covariances → a quadratic curve.

837d62d1fe3a.zh: 假設 $\Sigma_1=\Sigma_2$（形狀、胖瘦、旋轉完全一致），僅中心不同。Assume shared $\Sigma$ — same shape, different centres.
837d62d1fe3a.en: Assumes $\Sigma_1=\Sigma_2$, a shared $\Sigma$ (exactly the same shape, spread and rotation); only the centers differ.

d3ac137f59c2.zh: 決策邊界為直線/超平面，公式線性於 $x$ (linear in $x$)
d3ac137f59c2.en: The decision boundary is a straight line/hyperplane; the formula is linear in $x$

4ed1073caec6.zh: 參數少、穩健、適合小樣本 (few params, robust)
4ed1073caec6.en: Few parameters, robust, suited to small samples

4895b9afb4f9.zh: 若真實共變異數不同，會系統性偏誤 (biased if covariances differ)
4895b9afb4f9.en: If the true covariances differ, it is systematically biased

7acd8994c512.zh: 兩類相減 $\delta_1-\delta_2=0$ 為線性方程。Difference is linear → straight boundary.
7acd8994c512.en: Subtracting the two classes, $\delta_1-\delta_2=0$ is a linear equation.

4632dd1782ba.zh: 允許 $\Sigma_1\neq\Sigma_2$（每群胖瘦、旋轉各異）。Each class owns its $\Sigma_k$ — different spreads.
4632dd1782ba.en: Allows $\Sigma_1\neq\Sigma_2$: each cluster has its own $\Sigma_k$ (its own spread and rotation).

56f330d10765.zh: 決策邊界為拋物線/橢圓/雙曲線等二次曲線 (quadratic curves)
56f330d10765.en: The decision boundary is a quadratic curve such as a parabola/ellipse/hyperbola

935b3ad5235a.zh: 更彈性，但參數多、易過擬合 (flexible, more params)
935b3ad5235a.en: More flexible, but has more parameters and overfits easily

5bf51c34faba.zh: 每類需估 $O(d^2)$ 共變異數，小樣本慎用 ($O(d^2)$ covariance each)
5bf51c34faba.en: Each class needs an $O(d^2)$ covariance estimate; use with care on small samples

678597accd21.zh: 含 $x^T(\Sigma_1^{-1}-\Sigma_2^{-1})x$ → 二次項。Quadratic term survives → curved boundary.

be9401b49f5f.zh: LDA：直線切 · QDA：曲線切 — 同資料、不同假設、不同邊界
be9401b49f5f.en: LDA: straight cut · QDA: curved cut — same data, different assumptions, different boundaries

1d8b18098760.zh: LDA · 等共變異數 → 直線邊界

36d274a98ad9.zh: QDA · 異共變異數 → 二次曲線

40d1bb2bb81c.zh: 左：共變異數相同 → 橢圓等形狀，邊界筆直；右：胖瘦旋轉各異 → 邊界彎曲成二次曲線 · Left equal covariances → straight; right unequal → curved
40d1bb2bb81c.en: Left: equal covariances → ellipses of the same shape, straight boundary; right: different spreads and rotations → the boundary bends into a quadratic curve

ed0d7b44cd02.zh: 3 · Logistic 回歸：一顆神經元的誕生 Logistic Regression — A Single Neuron Is Born
ed0d7b44cd02.en: 3 · Logistic Regression: The Birth of a Single Neuron

1702d1a663e0.zh: 不猜「資料怎麼長」，直接建模 $P(Y=1\mid X)$。把線性分數 $z=w^Tx+b$ 塞進 Sigmoid 壓到 $[0,1]$，輸出就是機率。Skip $P(X\mid C)$; model $P(Y\mid X)$ directly via sigmoid on linear score.
1702d1a663e0.en: Don’t guess “what the data looks like” ($P(X\mid C)$); model $P(Y=1\mid X)$ directly. Feed the linear score $z=w^Tx+b$ into the sigmoid to squash it into $[0,1]$, and the output is a probability.

e70336e552c2.zh: 壓縮實數 → 機率 · squeeze ℝ → [0,1]

ba36c09833bc.zh: 線性分數經 Sigmoid 壓縮為機率，邊界仍線性但輸出平滑可校準 · Linear score → sigmoid → calibrated prob
ba36c09833bc.en: The sigmoid squashes the linear score into a probability; the boundary is still linear, but the output is smooth and can be calibrated

4cfecf55e862.zh: 生成 vs. 判別 · Generative vs. Discriminative

cbe8f26f3e87.zh: 貝氏/LDA 要估 $P(X\mid C)P(C)$ 兩大塊；Logistic 只估 $P(Y\mid X)$ 一塊，少做假設、少走彎路。Bayes/LDA estimate two pieces; Logistic estimates one — fewer assumptions.
cbe8f26f3e87.en: Bayes/LDA must estimate two big pieces, $P(X\mid C)P(C)$; logistic regression estimates only one, $P(Y\mid X)$: fewer assumptions, fewer detours.

1ec314ac87a0.zh: 這就是最老、最純的一顆人工神經元：線性加權 $+$ Sigmoid 非線性。疊很多顆就變深度網路。The oldest neuron: linear + sigmoid. Stack many → deep net.
1ec314ac87a0.en: This is the oldest, purest artificial neuron: a linear weighting $+$ a sigmoid nonlinearity. Stack lots of them and you get a deep network.

8e2e0e83aa5b.zh:
優：機率輸出可解釋、可校準；訓練凸優化、穩定。
缺：邊界仍線性，非線性資料需靠特徵工程或「升維＋核」。Pro: calibrated prob, convex. Con: linear boundary — need features/kernels for non-linear.
8e2e0e83aa5b.en:
Pros: the probability output is interpretable and can be calibrated; training is a convex optimization and stable.
Cons: the boundary is still linear, so nonlinear data needs feature engineering or “lifting to higher dimensions + kernels”.

27bd9c04db98.zh: 公式 · Sigmoid 與條件機率

e9ed9dd0d52f.zh: KNN 零訓練、零參數（除 $k$）：新樣本看最近 $k$ 個鄰居多數決。但「近」的定義決定一切——於是有度量學習。Zero training: classify by $k$ nearest votes. But “near” is everything — hence metric learning.
e9ed9dd0d52f.en: KNN has zero training and zero parameters (except $k$): a new sample takes a majority vote of its $k$ nearest neighbors. But the definition of “near” decides everything, hence metric learning.

949136556f6e.zh: 超參只有 $k$。$k$ 小 → 靈活但吵；$k$ 大 → 平滑但鈍。常用歐氏/餘弦距離。Only $k$. Small $k$ = flexible but noisy; large $k$ = smooth but blunt.
949136556f6e.en: The only hyperparameter is $k$. Small $k$ → flexible but noisy; large $k$ → smooth but blunt. Euclidean or cosine distance is common.

eeb5b22d15ad.en: Use an odd $k$ to avoid ties; choose $k$ by cross-validation; with class imbalance, use weighted voting $w=1/d$.

8f535dbd444c.en: A single tree has high variance and overfits easily; bagging lets each tree see a different subsample and feature subset, and averaging the decorrelated trees → variance drops sharply.

8d8b0fb3a0c4.zh: 二維蚊香混疊時，映射 $\phi(x)$ 到高維 Hilbert 空間變線性可分。核 $K(x,z)=\langle\phi(x),\phi(z)\rangle$ 讓我們不必算 $\phi$ 本身。Entangled spiral in 2D → linear in high-D. Kernel computes inner product without explicit $\phi$.
8d8b0fb3a0c4.en: When 2D data is entangled like a mosquito-coil spiral, mapping it with $\phi(x)$ into a high-dimensional Hilbert space makes it linearly separable. The kernel $K(x,z)=\langle\phi(x),\phi(z)\rangle$ means we never have to compute $\phi$ itself.

3073f6244da0.zh: 常用：RBF $K=\exp(-\gamma\|x-z\|^2)$（無限維）、多項式、線性。Popular: RBF (infinite-D), polynomial, linear.

cafa33e5aced.zh: 直覺：把紙揉起來切 · Scrunch the Paper
cafa33e5aced.en: Intuition: Scrunch Up the Paper and Cut

54768c0edd86.zh: 想像把混在一起的紅藍點畫在紙上，揉成球後從中間一刀切——攤平後在原平面看就是彎曲邊界。Draw mixed dots, scrunch paper, cut, unfold — curved boundary appears.
54768c0edd86.en: Imagine the mixed-up red and blue dots drawn on a sheet of paper. Scrunch it into a ball and slice straight through the middle: once you flatten it out again, the cut looks like a curved boundary on the original plane.

9ac0e4315494.zh: 核矩陣 $O(n^2)$ 記憶體與計算；超參 $\gamma, C$ 敏感。大數據時代常被深度網路取代，但在中小數據仍極強。$O(n^2)$ kernel matrix; sensitive $\gamma, C$. Still strong on small/medium data.
9ac0e4315494.en: The kernel matrix costs $O(n^2)$ memory and computation, and the hyperparameters $\gamma, C$ are sensitive. In the big-data era it is often replaced by deep networks, but on small and medium datasets it is still very strong.

f200f99a586f.zh: 對偶後僅內積 $\langle x_i,x_j\rangle$ 出現 → 可替換為核 $K(x_i,x_j)$。Dual uses only inner products → replace by kernel $K$.
f200f99a586f.en: After taking the dual, only inner products $\langle x_i,x_j\rangle$ appear → they can be replaced by a kernel $K$, i.e. $K(x_i,x_j)$.

77acec9565f3.en: Kernel trick: non-linear in low dimensions → linear in high dimensions; RBF even corresponds to an infinite-dimensional space

f6cf8fe2ac6e.zh: 每學一個家族就問三問：① 它假設世界長怎樣？② 它的邊界長怎樣？③ 它什麼時候會失靈？答得出來，才算真的會選模型。For each family ask: assumption? boundary shape? when does it fail? Answerable = truly understood.
f6cf8fe2ac6e.en: For each family you learn, ask three questions: ① What does it assume the world looks like? ② What does its boundary look like? ③ When does it fail? Only when you can answer these can you really choose models.
